title: Normalized coefficient-Hom unit for the ring in degree zero
statement: Let C be a small site, R and B sheaves of commutative rings, and phi:R -> B a ring-sheaf map. Let r be restriction of scalars, rc its extension to cochain complexes, and sigma:R[0] -> rc(B[0]) the map induced by phi. There exists a bifunctor F:C(B)^op -> (C(R) -> C(B)), a natural isomorphism c from its uncurried restriction to the R-valued product internal Hom after restricting its first input, and a natural B-linear chain map alpha:id -> rc;F(B[0],-). For every B-complex M, rc(alpha_M);c_(B[0],rc(M));Hom_R(sigma,rc(M)) equals the inverse of the specified evaluation-at-one isomorphism Hom_R(R[0],rc(M)) -> rc(M). No arbitrary augmented complexes, comparison u, resolution endofunctor, flatness or injectivity enter this statement.

source.place: Tag 099I (lemma-restriction-derived-complete-equivalence), first arrow of the final displayed composite; sites-cohomology.tex Section 0A8X for the product Hom differential.

proof.text: Obtain the separately additive coefficient-Hom bifunctor H with its explicit precomposition scalar action. Extend it to product Hom complexes G, using the structured product specification. Reuse the normalized private comparison retained from the existing restricted coefficient-Hom complex proof; its equation on the actual R-valued product projections is essential.

Construct the R-linear localized map m -> (b -> b*m) and transport it along the underived comparison. Its explicit scalar-action formula proves B-linearity. Set its product component to zero away from source degree zero and use the literal identity B[0]^0 = B at zero. Lift to the product, use zero internal Hom in every other source degree and the vanishing source differential to prove it is a chain map, and use localized naturality to prove naturality in M.

Compose the restricted unit with the normalized comparison and precomposition by sigma. Apply the canonical evaluation isomorphism and compute in each target degree at source degree zero. The single-complex comparison identifies the coefficient map with phi, so the local map evaluates phi(1)*m = m. Cancel the evaluation isomorphism to obtain the required normalization.

proof_origin.description: E6: explicit localized scalar-unit construction, the existing coefficient-complex product comparison with its normalization retained, and the degree-zero evaluation calculation following Stacks Tag 099I. All helper proofs are complete; the product specification is represented by equivalent structured data. The canonical single-complex identification at literal zero is the identity. The degree-zero unit family and the normalized evaluation API therefore use the underived normalization and evaluation laws directly, without a general transport theorem. The underived and complex projections share native internal-Hom endpoints. The consuming comparison and unit proofs unpack the product specification once and pass ProductHomComplexData directly, so projection laws use the same explicit data without repeated choice.

mathlib_searches.query: A restriction of scalars functor on sheaves of modules has coextension Hom from the coefficient ring as right adjoint with evaluation at one counit
mathlib_searches.results: ModuleCat.coextendScalars, ModuleCat.RestrictionCoextensionAdj.counit'_app, and PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars. The first two are for individual rings; none states a varying-ring-sheaf product Hom-complex unit or its normalized comparison.

mathlib_searches.query: An augmentation induces a natural map into the internal Hom complex by evaluation and restriction of scalars
mathlib_searches.results: CochainComplex.augment, ChainComplex.linearYonedaObj, and ModuleCat.RestrictionCoextensionAdj.counit'_app. The latter evaluates ordinary module Hom at one; no sheaf-valued product complex compatibility.

mathlib_searches.results: Existing coefficient bifunctor and product-complex extension are proved, but their public comparison theorem forgets the normalized projection equations. HomComplexUnitEvaluationNaturality handles the same-ring evaluation only. SheafCoinductionCounit has a proved scheme-specific adjunction, not the generic small-site normalized complex unit.
mathlib_searches.verdict: No duplicate; the unit compatibility is the missing proper step.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_coefficientHom_unit
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    {R B : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}} (φ : R ⟶ B) :
    let r := SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).map φ)
    let rc := r.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
    let σ : ringedSiteRingComplex R ⟶ rc.obj (ringedSiteRingComplex B) :=
      (HomologicalComplex.single _ (.up ℤ) 0).map
          (SheafOfModules.LocalizationCech.unitMap φ) ≫
        (HomologicalComplex.singleMapHomologicalComplex r (.up ℤ) 0).inv.app
          (SheafOfModules.unit ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj B))
    ∃ F : (ringedSiteComplex B)ᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteComplex R ⥤ ringedSiteComplex B,
      ∃ c : Functor.uncurry.obj F ⋙ rc ≅
          rc.op.prod (𝟭 _) ⋙ Functor.uncurry.obj (homComplexFunctor (R := R)),
        ∃ α : 𝟭 (ringedSiteComplex B) ⟶ rc ⋙ F.obj (op (ringedSiteRingComplex B)),
          ∀ M : ringedSiteComplex B,
            rc.map (α.app M) ≫ c.hom.app (op (ringedSiteRingComplex B), rc.obj M) ≫
                ((homComplexFunctor (R := R)).map σ.op).app (rc.obj M) =
              (by
                change rc.obj M ⟶ ((homComplexFunctor (R := R)).obj
                  (op (ringedSiteRingComplex R))).obj (rc.obj M)
                exact (ringedHomUnitEvaluationIso R (rc.obj M)).inv)
